title: IEEE 754 单精度拆解与边界值
expected_output:
=== IEEE 754 single precision ===
  layout: bit31=S, bit30..23=E (bias 127), bit22..0=M (hidden leading 1)
  value = (-1)^S * 1.M * 2^(E-127)

  --- ordinary values ---
  bits=0x3F800000  S=0  E=127  e_eff=    0  M=0x000000  normalized
  bits=0xBF800000  S=1  E=127  e_eff=    0  M=0x000000  normalized
  bits=0x3F000000  S=0  E=126  e_eff=   -1  M=0x000000  normalized
  bits=0x40000000  S=0  E=128  e_eff=    1  M=0x000000  normalized
  bits=0x40600000  S=0  E=128  e_eff=    1  M=0x600000  normalized
  bits=0x3DCCCCCD  S=0  E=123  e_eff=   -4  M=0x4CCCCD  normalized

  --- boundaries ---
  bits=0x00800000  S=0  E=  1  e_eff= -126  M=0x000000  normalized
        <- smallest positive NORMAL   (exponent field 1)
  bits=0x00000001  S=0  E=  0  e_eff= -126  M=0x000001  denormal
        <- smallest positive DENORMAL (exponent field 0)
  bits=0x007FFFFF  S=0  E=  0  e_eff= -126  M=0x7FFFFF  denormal
        <- largest DENORMAL: it glues onto the smallest normal

  --- why 0.1 is not exact ---
  0.1 stored as float  = 0.10000000149011611938
  0.1 stored as double = 0.10000000000000000555
  0.1 has an INFINITE binary expansion, so the last bit must be rounded

  --- bias arithmetic ---
  1.0f -> E=127 -> stored 127 -> e = 127-127 = 0 -> 1.0 * 2^0
  0.5f -> E=126 -> stored 126 -> e = 126-127 = -1 -> 1.0 * 2^-1
  denormal exponent is FIXED at -126 (bias minus one), which is why it glues on
